chunks: And by his chain, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Baseer who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who emancipated half of his slave girl, then he contracted her upon the other half after that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him stipulate upon her that if she is unable to pay her installments, she will be returned to slavery regarding half of her body.' He said: 'If he wishes, there will be for him her service for a day, and for her a day.' I said: 'Is it for her that she marries in that state?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until she pays off all that is upon her regarding half of her body.'

key_terms.رَقَبَتِهَا: Her body (referring to the slave's value)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a partially freed slave girl to marry or return to slavery?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the contractual mechanics of partial manumission, establishing that the owner may stipulate a reversion to slavery for half the neck if the slave girl defaults on her kataba payments. This ruling highlights the balance between the slave's path to freedom and the owner's financial rights, specifically noting that marriage is prohibited until the entire debt for the remaining half is fully settled, ensuring the contract's integrity.

en.hubeali: And by his chain, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a man who emancipated half of his slave girl, then he contracted her upon the other half after that. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let him stipulated upon her that if she was frustrated from her installments, so she would be returned into the slavery with regards to half of her slavery. So if he so desires to, there would be for him, her services for a day, and for her would be a day, if he has not contracted her’. I said, ‘Is it for her that she gets married, being in that state?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, until she has paid off the entirety of what is upon her with regards to half of her slavery’.
